string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital of the People’s Republic of China and the nation’s political and cultural center. It is an ancient capital with more than 3,000 years of history, blending precious imperial heritage and modern urban vitality. Famous landmarks include the Forbidden City, the Great Wall and the Temple of Heaven. As a major international exchange hub, it hosts numerous cultural events and top research institutions. It perfectly carries forward traditional Chinese civilization while embracing new technological development.

Shanghai is a centrally administered municipality at the estuary of the Yangtze River. It is China’s leading international economic, financial and trade center, well-known for its open and inclusive culture. The Bund and Lujiazui show the contrast between classic colonial architecture and cutting-edge skyscrapers. As the core of the Yangtze River Delta economic zone, it attracts global enterprises and talents. It keeps balancing rapid economic growth with cultural inheritance and urban renewal.

Chongqing is the only municipality directly under the central government in western China. It lies on the upper Yangtze River and is widely called the “Mountain City” because of its layered hilly landscape. It became a municipality in 1997 and serves as a key transportation and industrial hub in southwest China. It is famous for hotpot, unique night views and Dazu Rock Carvings. It supports regional development and connects inland areas with the Yangtze waterway.

Tianjin is one of China’s four municipalities, acting as the important gateway to Beijing. It sits beside the Haihe River and faces the Bohai Sea. Founded in 1404, it has a long history as a port city. It mixes Western-style historic buildings and modern industrial zones. Its busy port supports logistics and manufacturing across North China. It works closely with Beijing in the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei coordinated development plan.
